title: 1 day ago •Driver News Final Statistics Betray Graham Rahal’s Progress This Season The lead Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing driver (photo) earned three podium finishes this season but finished 16th in the final season standings due to inconsistency.
excerpt:
Driver News

1 day ago

Graham Rahal’s rocky NTT INDYCAR SERIES season was capsulized by the last-lap happenings in the XPEL Grand Prix at Road America on June 21.

Rahal had passed Will Power for third place in Turn 6 only to have Power’s trailing car make contact with his approaching Turn 12. The impact sent Rahal sliding to the outside barrier, where it ricocheted into the gravel barrier.

Rahal (photo, top) had been on pace to be the highest-finishing Honda driver. Instead, it was a crushing 23rd-place finish.

“Two corners away from (a podium finish),” Rahal said with a sigh at the season-ending event at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

Rahal’s results in the 18-race campaign included a healthy amount of feast and more than his share of famine. The driver of Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing’s No. 15 Honda had three top-three finishes, but they were offset by six finishes in the 20s, including the one at Road America that could have been in the former category.

Only six drivers had more podium finishes, and had Power not knocked him sideways at Road America, he would have matched Team Penske’s Scott McLaughlin in that category. Series champion Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing and Arrow McLaren’s Christian Lundgaard led the series with seven podiums each, while Andretti Global’s Kyle Kirkwood and Team Penske’s David Malukas had six apiece. Andretti Global’s Power had five.

Rahal’s podium finishes came in the Children’s of Alabama Indy Grand Prix at Barber Motorsports Park (photo, above), the Sonsio Grand Prix on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and the Chevrolet Detroit Grand Prix. He qualified third and finished ninth in the Good Ranchers 250 at Phoenix Raceway in the season’s second race. In street racing, he qualified and finished ninth in the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham, Ontario, and led a season-high 12 laps in the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C.

Yet, despite how well Rahal and his RLL crew performed in some events, their struggles at others left them 16th in the standings.

“So, while people want to discount us, I don't think that that's necessarily fair on a year like this year,” Rahal said. “We had a lot of good opportunities, but what our weakness was on one weekend we'd be on the podium, the next weekend we'd finish 23rd.

“Our highs were high, our lows were very, very low, and that's the frustration for me.”

Another example of that was in the August weekend in the OnlyBulls Grand Prix at Portland. Rahal qualified eighth – “(That position was) way better than I thought I was going to qualify,” he said – but he finished a lap off the pace in 23rd place.

“So, things like that (were) quite frustrating,” he said.

The six-time race winner in this series had already turned his focus to next season by the time the series arrived at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca for the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey, the last race of the year. There, Rahal said he and the team will have their short oval package high on the list of areas to improve given their struggles at Nashville Superspeedway and the Milwaukee Mile in the second half of the season.

“I’m very decided to (2027) already to try to make sure we’re making the right moves, doing the right things,” Rahal said, adding that RLL will reset with two full-season entries (for Rahal and Louis Foster). “We’ve tried to keep up this three-car thing for many years, often at the great expense of our team owners. Just need to reset and rethink.

“It’s a very important time of the year to make sure that we're doing the right things.”

title: 1 day ago •Driver News Indianapolis 500 Folk Hero ‘Jigger’ Sirois Dies at 91
excerpt:
Leon Duray “Jigger” Sirois, who became part of Indianapolis 500 folklore by nearly earning an improbable pole for the 1969 race, died Sept. 23. He was 91.

Sirois, a native of Shelby, Indiana, made no starts in “The Greatest Spectacle in Racing” despite attempting to qualify every year from 1969-75. But his close call at earning the top starting spot in unique circumstances in May 1969 became a legendary story in the history of the world’s greatest race.

Midget car standout Sirois drew first in line to attempt to qualify on Pole Day, May 17, 1969, in the No. 14 Gerhardt-Offenhauser owned by California car dealer Myron Caves. After a long rain delay, Sirois entered the 2.5-mile oval late in the afternoon to make the first four-lap qualification attempt of the day.

His first three laps ranged between 160 and 162 mph, but Caves waved off the final lap of the run due to a perceived lack of speed, negating the run. Moments later, Arnie Knepper began his qualifying attempt, but rain began to fall during his warmup laps and continued, washing out all track activity for the rest of the weekend.

If Sirois’ final lap had not been waved off, he would have been the lone qualifier of the weekend and have sat on the coveted provisional pole for that week, perhaps even holding it through Bump Day the next weekend and starting the race from the top spot. Sirois’ second and third attempts the next weekend also were waved off due to lack of speed or mechanical problems, and he didn’t qualify for the race.

Qualification rules were changed in 1971 to guarantee all cars in line on the first day of qualifying at least one chance to make the field during the first round, ending any chance of another “Jigger” story.

Sirois continued to attempt to qualify for the “500” every year through 1975, including the sluggish Jack Adams Turbine in 1970. It was the last qualifying attempt ever for the Indianapolis 500 by a turbine-engine car. He was the second alternate for the 1974 race, falling just short of making the field.

The failure to qualify at Indianapolis belied Sirois’ skill at many levels of open-wheel racing.

Sirois failed to qualify for the five USAC Champ Car races he entered in 1967 driving for team owner Bob Cavanaugh. But he attracted strong attention from Indianapolis 500 car owners in 1968 after he was forced to withdraw from the inaugural USAC Champ Car race at Michigan International Speedway due to clutch failure while running as high as second in low-budget equipment.

He made 10 USAC Champ Car starts, with a best finish of fifth in 1969 at Phoenix. He also finished third – in a turbine-engine car – behind winner A.J. Foyt and Knepper in the rain-shortened Ted Horn Memorial USAC National Dirt Car Championship race in September 1972 at DuQuoin, Illinois.

Sirois enjoyed the most success in midgets, primarily racing around the Chicago area. He won four championships in 1961, including the UARA midget title. He was inducted into the National Midget Racing Hall of Fame in 2013.

One of the most popular veteran drivers, Sirois returned to IMS in May frequently to meet fans and media members, always well-liked for his geniality and courtesy. His sportsmanship surrounding the fateful decision to wave off his 1969 qualifying attempt – he never once blamed Caves or his crew – led the American Auto Racing Writers & Broadcasters Association (AARWBA) to create the annual “Jigger Award” to honor the year’s “hard luck” driver during qualifying. Sirois was the first recipient in 1969.

Sirois was born into the sport. His father, Earl “Frenchy” Sirois, was a longtime Indianapolis 500 mechanic who worked on the winning cars of Lee Wallard, Sam Hanks and Jimmy Bryan during his 40-year career. Sirois was named after two-time “500” pole winner Leon Duray.

The legendary nickname “Jigger” referred to two-time Indy 500-winning riding mechanic Jigger Johnson, a family friend. Sirois’ older sister also called him by that name.

Sirois suffered from a stutter that began during a tornado scare near his hometown of Shelby when he was 3 years old. He began to manage his stutter in his mid-60s after receiving speech therapy and worked tirelessly to promote awareness and treatment of stuttering disorders in youth.

title: Scott Dixon To Drive No. 6, Felix Rosenqvist No. 7 for Arrow McLaren
excerpt:
Pato O’Ward Staying in No. 5, Ryan Hunter-Reay Back in No. 31 at Indy

The Arrow McLaren IndyCar Team announced Sept. 23 its driver numbers for its new lineup entering the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season.

Pato O'Ward will continue in the No. 5, while Scott Dixon will take over the No. 6 entry, and Felix Rosenqvist will drive the No. 7. In the team's additional Indy 500 entry, Ryan Hunter-Reay will continue with the No. 31 next May.

Additionally, Arrow McLaren unveiled a new font style for car numbers in line with the rebrand McLaren Racing rolled out Sept. 22 that will go into effect in January 2027.

"We're excited to begin our next chapter in 2027," Team Principal Tony Kanaan said. "This team has continued to raise the bar year after year, and with Pato, Scott, Felix and Ryan in the cockpit, we believe we have the tools to achieve our goals. While fans will have to wait a little longer to see the 2027 liveries, today's announcement offers a fun glimpse of what lies ahead."

Dixon is set to sport a new car number in INDYCAR SERIES competition for the first time in more than two decades after competing in his familiar No. 9 for all but one of the past 24 seasons (No. 1 in 2004). Fresh off his Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge victory in 2026, Rosenqvist returns to the No. 7 entry, the same number he drove during his first two seasons with Arrow McLaren from 2021-22.

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season starts Sunday, March 7 in St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Featured Inside Line: 2026 Moment That Will Matter Most in 2027?
excerpt:
Featured

2 DAYS AGO

Today’s question: What moment from the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season will matter the most in the 2027 season?

Curt Cavin: I’d like to highlight a stretch of late-season races where Will Power earned three consecutive podium finishes (third each at Portland, Markham and Washington). That was part of seven races in a row in which Power (photo, above) led laps, and he ended the year with five top-three finishes, the fifth-highest individual total and only two off that of series champion Alex Palou. Why is it important to single out three races of a driver who finished 11th in the point standings? Because Power is a two-time series champion who figures to be massively confident heading into his second season with Andretti Global. Even if Power doesn’t win a third title, he can be the help teammate Kyle Kirkwood needs to overthrow Palou. It’s worth noting that Andretti Global’s combination of Kirkwood, Power and Marcus Ericsson combined for 13 podium finishes, tied with Team Penske for the most among teams in 2026. Don’t be surprised if they gang up on Palou next season.

Eric Smith: I think the way David Malukas lost the Indy 500 in May could help him win the “500” next year. That’s my moment because the final lap of this past year’s Indy 500 is arguably the moment of the entire 2026 season. Alex Palou admitted that his 2021 Indy 500 defeat to Helio Castroneves taught him what he needed to know to win the 2025 race. Malukas (photo, above) came close -- finishing as the closest second-place finisher in Indy 500 history. It was also his second consecutive runner-up finish in the race. Thirty-six drivers have finished second in the Indy 500 and gone on to win it, with nine of those drivers earning their runner-up finish the year before their first “500” victory. Now, with Malukas driving a Team Penske car, he should be in contention. More importantly, he has the experience and knowledge from his recent defeats to close the deal and capture the 2027 Indy 500 victory.

Arni Sribhen: For me, it’s the driver movement at Arrow McLaren and Chip Ganassi Racing — a sequence of moves that could turn three separate moments into one massive storyline, with the biggest piece still waiting to fall into place. At the center of it: Scott Dixon and Christian Lundgaard. Call it a “trade” if you want, because that’s exactly how this is going to be viewed. Sure, both teams still have nine other organizations to race next season. But make no mistake, every Lundgaard result at his new home will be measured against what Dixon (photo, above) does at his. And if Lundgaard follows up with another title-contending season? The comparisons will get loud. Then there’s the history. These two organizations aren’t exactly exchanging Christmas cards. The Alex Palou saga made that clear, and there’s been no shortage of bad blood – particularly between the people running the show. So, keep an eye on this one. Because by the end of 2027, when we look back at the Dixon-Lundgaard “trade,” one of these organizations could be doing a whole lot more laughing than the other.

Paul Kelly: The success of the new street races in Arlington and Washington rank very high for me, both short term and long term. In the short view, the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (photo, top) will continue to prosper and grow into one of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ tentpole events next season. Don’t be surprised if it ranks with the Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach as one of the series’ unofficial “majors” besides the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. While it’s unlikely the series returns to Washington next year, the overwhelming success of that race provides a template for excellence for promoters of every street race in the series, and you can be sure those lessons will be applied elsewhere. Plus, INDYCAR stages street races arguably better than any series in North America, and that successful model can be borrowed from Arlington and Washington and taken to another city. The series badly needs a race in the Northeast, so the streets of Philadelphia (sorry, Bruce Springsteen!), anyone? How about a Mile High fight on the streets of Denver?

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Driver News ‘500’ Reality Sinks In for Felix Rosenqvist After Seeing Borg Likeness
excerpt:
Felix Rosenqvist traveled to Tryon, North Carolina, this week to see his face that will be added to one of the most exclusive pieces of hardware in motorsports.

On Sept. 22, artist William Behrends unveiled Rosenqvist’s sculpted clay likeness that will serve as the bas-relief portrait on the Borg-Warner Trophy. The iconic hardware carries the likeness of every Indianapolis 500 winner, creating a visual history of the race dating to its inaugural running in 1911.

“It’s been quite the experience,” Rosenqvist said. “Such a cool, unique little trip here, getting to meet Will (Behrends) and his family. It’s kind of a rare thing to experience. I never thought I would be sculpted. I think it’s not a thing people really expect to do in their lifetime.

“He did a hell of a job with it. To do all the details right was very impressive to see. Even my little imperfections we all have, they’re all there.”

Rosenqvist earned his place on the Borg-Warner Trophy by winning the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge on May 24. Driving the No. 60 SiriusXM Honda for Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian, he made a daring move on the final lap, riding the high line against the wall exiting Turn 4 on Lap 200 and powering past David Malukas in the No. 12 Verizon Team Penske Chevrolet just yards before the Yard of Bricks start-finish line.

Rosenqvist won by .0233 of a second, the closest finish in Indianapolis 500 history. The race also featured a record-setting 70 lead changes. The victory came in Rosenqvist’s eighth Indianapolis 500 start, made him the 77th different winner of the race and earned him a record $4.34 million in prize money.

His victory initially took him on a media tour before the NTT INDYCAR SERIES returned to competition the following weekend on the streets of Detroit. With the season over, Rosenqvist said the trip to Tryon felt like “celebration 2.0.”

“It becomes more real now,” Rosenqvist said. “It’s one of those kind of victories that just always stays. No one’s ever going to be able to take it away from you, which I think is also why it’s such a relief to win this race, because we all dream about it, we all think about it, but we all know also how hard to win it.

“So, when you finally get it, it’s just like such a relief, and the fact that you also get imprinted on a trophy doesn’t hurt. Like, no one can undo what you did.”

Now, Rosenqvist is part of that history. He also brings a distinction no previous winner has brought to the trophy: He is the first Indianapolis 500 winner depicted with a full beard.

“That’s almost unbelievable,” Behrends said. “I mean, how can that happen? It’s just astounding.”

Behrends, who began sculpting drivers for the Borg-Warner Trophy in 1990, wanted the beard represented without making it the first feature people noticed.

“I had to kind of play around with the clay and figure out how I was going to do that, but I think we got it,” he said.

Rosenqvist found the distinction of being the first bearded driver on the Borg as crazy but believes he became a trendsetter.

“I think it’s the most mind-blowing fact because I feel like everyone has a beard,” Rosenqvist said. “Like, out of my friends, probably at least half of them have a beard.”

Six previous winners have been depicted with mustaches: Jules Goux (1913), René Thomas (1914), Gaston Chevrolet (1920), Wilbur Shaw (1937, 1939, 1940), Mauri Rose (1941, 1947, 1948) and Bobby Rahal (1986). None had a beard.

Behrends has sculpted two other Swedish Indianapolis 500 winners, 1999 winner Kenny Brack and 2022 winner Marcus Ericsson. American Josef Newgarden won back-to-back years in 2023 and 2024 while Spaniard Alex Palou won in 2025. Rosenqvist’s likeness gave him another opportunity to capture details that make each driver unique.

“One thing I like about his face, Felix has got a very strong jaw,” Behrends said. “He has a very Swedish jaw, so I like that. It’s a very strong, kind of angular face, a different-shaped face, by far, than Alex (Palou) or Josef’s (Newgarden), but very strong.

“Then he says: ‘I got his nose right. That’s a family nose.’ Apparently, his grandfather, father and now his daughter have that nose.”

Rosenqvist also noticed another detail Behrends captured: His right ear sits slightly higher than his left. He also was blown away seeing his likeness in three dimensions. That made the experience more personal than simply seeing his name on a trophy.

“I think the details are what make it come alive,” Rosenqvist said. “Because that’s literally what makes you, you. I think the cool thing was because we’ve all seen pictures of ourselves, but to see like a 3D version of yourself and to be able to look around and walk behind him, look out behind the ears and all the kind of things you never could do, it’s a little bit of an eerie experience.

“He’s definitely a pro, and he made it definitely worthy to be on the trophy.”

The significance extends beyond Rosenqvist himself. He and his wife, Emille, welcomed their first child, Stella, in May. Rosenqvist showed his likeness to his wife on a live phone video during the studio visit (photo, above).

Rosenqvist hopes his place on the Borg-Warner Trophy, which is housed daily at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Hall of Fame Museum, will eventually become part of his family’s connection to the race.

“Maybe our grandkids will go check it out every now and then, or maybe it’ll be a tradition where we go to Indy if we don’t live there,” Rosenqvist said. “It’ll be a cool little family thing for us.

“Whatever happens, if my daughter or if I have a son in the future, or whatever happens, they decide to do something completely different, we always have that piece of history in our family to go back and say, ‘Hey, your grandpa did that,’ which is very rare to have that possibility. It’s very unique to have that opportunity.”

Photo credits: Scott R. LePage

title: Historic Season Unleashes New Era of Growth for NTT INDYCAR SERIES
excerpt:
The 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season was historic, record-breaking and game-changing for North America’s premier open-wheel racing series. From massive audience gains to soaring attendance, booming digital engagement and world-class competition, the series leaped forward into a new position of prominence and impact across the sporting landscape.

“This is an incredible new era for the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, defined by growth, energy and momentum,” Penske Entertainment President & CEO Mark Miles said. “Our partnership with FOX Sports has raised the bar for our sport, and in turn we’ve invested in new events and opportunities to accelerate our already immense progress. Alongside our teams and partners, our commitment to maintain and expand one of the fastest growth curves in all of sports is unmatched.”

A look at the season, by the facts and numbers:

Surging Viewership

The NTT INDYCAR SERIES reached an average audience of 1.68 million viewers on FOX across an 18-race schedule. This represents the largest average viewership in almost two decades, dating back to the 2008 season. In total, nine races saw an average audience of more than 1 million viewers, also the most since the 2008 season.

The historic Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. provided particularly stellar viewership, reaching a peak audience of 3.5 million people. This was the highest tune-in for a non-Indy 500 race since 1995. With all coverage on FOX combined, the NTT INDYCAR SERIES made a record 23 appearances on broadcast television in 2026.

Rising Attendance

Race weekend attendance increased by approximately 20 percent, benchmarked by another grandstand sellout at the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge and a massive crowd of 215,000 people across the Freedom 250 Grand Prix race weekend.

Additional highlights included a record-breaking weekend at the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg and a record-tying weekend at the Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach. INDYCAR’s return to Phoenix Raceway resulted in doubled Saturday attendance for the promoter and additional buzz surrounding an action-packed motorsport weekend. The inaugural Java House Grand Prix of Arlington also declared a grandstand sellout on race morning, highlighting incredible interest in the new event powered by a joint venture between INDYCAR, the Dallas Cowboys and REV Entertainment.

Impressive Digital Gains

INDYCAR’s social channels reached new heights in 2026, led by notable milestones in engagement and video consumption. The 2026 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge delivered the most popular digital day in NTT INDYCAR SERIES history, with more than 1.5 million engagements. In addition, there were more than 250 million video views across social and digital channels, also a new record.

The INDYCAR App powered by NTT DATA delivered a record-breaking performance in 2026 with the highest-ever average race day users across the season and a nearly 20 percent increase in screen views compared to 2025. The immersive relationship with NTT also celebrated a monumental moment in May, as NTT, Inc., together with NTT DATA Group Corporation, announced continued sponsorship of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

INDYCAR’s YouTube channel saw significant growth for the 2026 season with a 58 percent increase in watch time, a 41 percent increase in view duration and a nearly 70 percent growth in livestream views.

The new, digital-first docuseries “ALL IN: INDYCAR” also expanded the sport’s dedicated shoulder programming and reached a new and younger audience. Produced by INDYCAR in tandem with FOX Sports and Tom Brady’s Shadow Lion, “ALL IN: INDYCAR” racked up more than 6 million views on YouTube, averaging almost 500,000 views an episode.

Merchandise Sales Soar

NTT INDYCAR SERIES merchandise flew off the shelves across the season, with a nearly 40 percent increase in race weekend sales. The series set a new non-Indy 500 sales record in Arlington, only to break it months later on the streets of Washington. New and expanded lines were unveiled with brands such as Homefield, True Brand, Flag & Anthem, Under Armour, Travis Matthew, Lululemon and more.

World-Class Competition

The NTT INDYCAR SERIES once again featured intense, high-speed drama and competition, powered by a global field of elite drivers. Chip Ganassi Racing’s Alex Palou, at just 29 years old, became the youngest five-time champion in INDYCAR SERIES history. Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian’s Felix Rosenqvist earned his first Indy 500 victory in the closest finish in the race’s storied century-plus history.

Competition remained fierce throughout the 18-race schedule, with eight different drivers winning races and a record 20 drivers making at least one Firestone Fast Six qualifying appearance. In total, nine different race teams were represented on the podium in 2026.

IR-28 Unveiled

With momentum on its side, the NTT INDYCAR SERIES also showcased its commitment to the future with the unveiling of the IR-28 car that will be introduced for the start of the 2028 season. Lighter, faster and built to break track records, the IR-28 will encourage more wheel-to-wheel action through improved raceability, while its innovative and modern design will also engage a new generation of fans.

“The IR-28 unveil was a massive milestone for the sport, and it has been incredible to get so much positive feedback from both our drivers and our fans,” INDYCAR President J. Douglas Boles said. “To capitalize on our momentum, we need to be constantly innovating and look toward the future, and the IR-28 reflects our commitment to this mindset.”

The IR-28 also showcases the continued commitment of Chevy and Honda as INDYCAR’s Official Engine Manufacturers (OEM). The 2026 calendar year started with news that both partners had committed to new OEM agreements running multiple years, reflecting the upward trajectory of the sport and continued investments in its growth.

Stay tuned for more NTT INDYCAR SERIES updates as the sport turns the page on the 2026 season and prepares for an action-packed and highly anticipated 2027.

title: Scott McLaughlin Pleased To Complete Road Back to Victory Lane
excerpt:
Scott McLaughlin never doubted he would return to victory lane. The question was, how long it would take?

McLaughlin ended the longest winless streak of his professional racing career earlier this month in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ season finale at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. The victory snapped a 36-race drought that capped a season of rebuilding for the New Zealander and Team Penske.

The road back began long before the checkered flag fell at Laguna Seca. McLaughlin entered the 2025 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge fifth in the championship standings, only 14 points behind Kyle Kirkwood for second place. McLaughlin had four top-six finishes in the opening five races and appeared to be a legitimate championship contender.

Then everything changed. Series officials discovered illegal attenuators on the cars of teammates Will Power and Josef Newgarden before Indianapolis 500 qualifying. The fallout led to the departures of team president Tim Cindric, managing director Ron Ruzewski and general manager Kyle Moyer.

Moyer was McLaughlin’s strategist. Cindric and Ruzewski had been calling strategy for Newgarden and Power, respectively. The changes impacted all three cars as the organization worked to rebuild its competition structure. Team Penske eventually found its footing, winning two of the final three races of the 2025 season, one by Power the other by Newgarden, but the transition carried into the offseason.

More changes followed before the start of 2026. Jonathan Diuguid shed the interim label and became Team Penske president. He also moved into the strategist role for Newgarden, with Luke Mason transitioning to engineer. Ben Bretzman, McLaughlin’s longtime engineer since he came to the series for the 2020 season finale and full-time from 2021 onward, took on an engineering management role across all three cars.

For the first time in his NTT INDYCAR SERIES career, McLaughlin had a new race engineer in Raul Prados. He also had a new spotter in David Hunt. Cindric returned for race weekends as McLaughlin’s strategist.

Prados brought extensive sports car experience to the No. 3 Team Penske Chevrolet. He had been competing in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship since 2017 and was part of a championship-winning program before returning to INDYCAR competition. The adjustment took time.

“This is the most competitive category I've ever been in in my life as well,” McLaughlin said. “Even more so than any of the years of Supercars and stuff. I think this category is super tough right now, super tight and you need everything to go right.”

The breakthrough came with a late-June test at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course. With limited testing opportunities, a full day’s worth of work allowed the team to fix a communication barrier.

McLaughlin (photo, above) had six top-10 finishes through the first 10 races of the season entering that test and an average finish of 9.3. Over the final eight races, his average finish improved to eighth despite a 22nd-place result in Washington, where he crashed while battling Kirkwood for the lead with fewer than 20 laps remaining. Remove that result and the numbers tell an even better story. McLaughlin’s average finish over the final eight races would have been 5.5.

The improvement was not simply a matter of results. The No. 3 team began giving McLaughlin a car capable of competing at the front on different types of circuits.

McLaughlin finished fourth at Portland International Raceway and second and fourth in the doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile before breaking through with season finale win. The run gave McLaughlin three consecutive top-four finishes to close the season and, perhaps more importantly, confidence that the pieces were finally coming together.

Perhaps the biggest piece was he and Prado’s communication.

McLaughlin knows he can be fiery on the radio. Prados was still learning how to translate those messages into changes on the car. Sometimes, McLaughlin’s fiery description of a problem led Prados to make a larger adjustment than necessary.

A car that was already capable of running at the front might need a small change to remain there. Instead, the team occasionally made a larger swing in search of the solution. They eventually found a better way to communicate.

“We went back to the old printed-off track maps, and I marked on each section of the track where it was really bad or a 10 out of 10 and put it in the truck good,” McLaughlin said.

It was a simple solution to a complicated problem. Instead of relying solely on radio conversations during the intensity of a race weekend, McLaughlin and Prados created a shared language for identifying where the car needed work and how much work it needed. That process helped turn a new driver-engineer pairing into one capable of fighting at the front. The result was visible at Laguna Seca.

The victory did more than close a difficult chapter. It provided evidence that the changes inside Team Penske were beginning to produce the results everyone expected from one of INDYCAR’s premier organizations.

“I think we're getting our way back to where we want to be,” McLaughlin said.

title: Who Were Most Improved Drivers of 2026 Season?
excerpt:
The NTT INDYCAR SERIES does not single out most improved drivers in a given year, but there certainly were worthy candidates among the current 25 full-season participants.

Some of the drivers in the category have elevated themselves to championship contenders while others have raised their status within their teams. Some are younger than others some have more experience than others.

Some have race wins on their resume; others appear to be winners in waiting.

Some made more year-over-year progress than others, but all pass the eye test.

Becoming Title Contenders

Kyle Kirkwood

Andretti Global’s 27-year-old Floridian finished second in the standings, so he gets the honor of being highlighted first. No one doubted Kirkwood could be a star in this series – he was one in each of the junior categories – but he elevated his game this year and gave reigning series champion Alex Palou competition. Kirkwood (photo, above) had the points lead through four races.

Fourth in last year’s standings, Kirkwood got this season off to a strong start, posting top-10 finishes in 12 of the first 13 races, including four podium finishes and the victory in the inaugural street race in Arlington, Texas. Later in the year, Kirkwood won the highly anticipated street race in Washington.

Kirkwood knows he and others still have a lot of ground to make up on Palou, who has won five of the past six series championships and has shown no signs of slowing down. But Kirkwood took another big step in his fifth season in the series and is positioned to take another step up in 2027.

Christian Lundgaard

The 25-year-old Danish driver had a season similar to Kirkwood’s, and he also made people realize how close he is to hoisting an Astor Challenge Cup. Also like Kirkwood, Lundgaard (photo, above) improved two important positions in the standings, jumping from fifth to third in points.

There were lots of examples of Lundgaard’s brilliance on road courses – he won at Indianapolis Motor Speedway and Road America – but with Arrow McLaren he also had podium finishes on the streets of St. Petersburg (third place) and Washington (second).

But where Lundgaard improved the most this season was on short ovals. His best outing was finishing a career-best third and sixth in the doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile. He also finished 10th at World Wide Technology Raceway. If he can continue to make that type of progress on the ovals, he’ll become an even stronger championship contender with his new team in 2027.

David Malukas

There were some who questioned Team Penske’s decision to bring on the 24-year-old Chicago native for 2026, but those questions have disappeared.

Malukas (photo, above) narrowly lost the closest “500” finish in history, placing second for one of his four times this season. At the Milwaukee Mile, he led a career-high 93 laps in the second race, and he led at least 25 laps in four other races.

Most surprising was that Malukas scored more points this season than his two more experienced teammates. Malukas finished fifth in the standings, with Scott McLaughlin sixth and Josef Newgarden eighth.

Malukas finished 11th in last year’s standings with AJ Foyt Racing.

Veterans Moving Up

Perhaps “Comeback Driver of the Year” better fits Marcus Ericsson’s season.

Simply put, 2025 was a low point for the 36-year-old Swede (photo, top), who finished 20th in the standings – not the place for a one-time Indianapolis 500 winner in his seventh season, and he knew it.

Ericsson vowed that his third season with Andretti Global would be better, and it was. He was the biggest statistical gainer, vaulting to seventh in the standings, an improvement of 13 positions.

The Swede started the season by qualifying on the front row in two of the first three races – both street races – and won the first pole of his career at the new event in Arlington, Texas. He also led laps in each of the first three races and in five races during the season.

Ericsson closed the season with seven consecutive top-10 finishes, including the fifth win of his career (in the new street event in Markham, Ontario). He desperately wanted to match his career best with a sixth-place standings finish, but Team Penske’s Scott McLaughlin secured the position by winning the season-ending race at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

Rinus VeeKay won his first and only series race in 2021 and has had three years where he qualified on the front row for the “500,” but this was easily his most complete season.

VeeKay, 26, finished ninth in the season-opening race in St. Petersburg, finished a career-best sixth at Indy and closed the second half of the season with one of the sport’s strongest kicks.

VeeKay (photo, above) posted seven top-10 finishes in the final 12 races, highlighted by finishes of third and seventh in the doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile. He also delivered three fourth-place finishes (at World Wide Technology Raceway, Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course and Portland International Raceway).

The product of VeeKay’s success was a career-best 10th-place finish in the standings, two positions better than his previous best seasons (in 2021 and 2022). He also gave Juncos Hollinger Racing its best standings result – its previous mark had been 16th by Callum Ilott in 2023.

Not To Be Overlooked

Kyffin Simpson’s third season with Chip Ganassi Racing easily was his best, and it continued his climb to series relevance.

Simpson, 21, had his best run at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, qualifying in the seventh position for the “500” and finishing 14th, both personal highs by a wide margin. For the season, he delivered a pair of top-five finishes (fourth at Road America, fifth in Washington) and a personal-best eight top-10 finishes.

Simpson (photo, above) finished 13th in the standings, just four points behind teammate and six-time series champion Scott Dixon. Simpson had finished 21st and 17th in his two previous seasons, so this was another four-position gain.

title: Kyle Kirkwood Still Focused on Improvement Despite Career Year
excerpt:
Kyle Kirkwood has produced steady progress since he entered the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in 2022.

He finished 24th as a rookie with AJ Foyt Racing, then climbed to 11th, seventh and fourth in his first three seasons with Andretti Global. This year, he took another step and finished runner-up behind five-time series champion Alex Palou, who earned his record-tying fourth straight title.

“It’s big,” Kirkwood said. “I hope people consider us as the second-best team. We have a lot to build off of, right? We made a huge jump year over year. Now second in the championship.”

Kirkwood and Andretti Global face the challenge of not only making up 86 points on Palou, the final margin this past season, but passing him in the standings. No one has done that since 2022.

“I’ll look at myself, figure out which tracks I need to be better at, whether it’s just driving, performance, but also mistakes,” Kirkwood said.

Palou has won five of the last six titles. His 25 career victories include 17 on permanent road courses, five on street circuits and three on ovals. Kirkwood has seven career wins, with six coming on street circuits. He is winless in 32 series starts on permanent road courses and has one victory in 26 oval starts. Those numbers point to where Kirkwood can make his biggest gains.

Kirkwood has been one of the series’ strongest street-course drivers, but Palou narrowed that advantage this season. Three of Palou’s five career street-course victories came in 2026, at St. Petersburg, Long Beach and Detroit.

Permanent road courses offer Kirkwood the biggest opportunity. He dominated those circuits before reaching INDYCAR SERIES competition. Of his 41 victories in the junior formulas, 32 came on permanent road courses. He has yet to win on one in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, although his results this season showed progress.

Kirkwood finished in the top 10 at all six permanent road-course races in 2026: Barber Motorsports Park, the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course, Road America, Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course, Portland International Raceway and WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

Andretti Global also has work to do on those tracks. Alexander Rossi gave the team its most recent permanent road-course victory in July 2022 at IMS. The team has four permanent road-course victories since 2020.

The Indianapolis 500 also remains a priority. Kirkwood identified IMS as the biggest area where Andretti Global can improve, noting that the organization’s average finish there is its worst at any track on the schedule lately.

Since 2020, Andretti has just one top-five finish at Indianapolis, with a best result of fifth in 2022. The team has recorded only three top-10 “500” finishes since 2021, along with seven results of 30th or worse and just 69 laps led in that span.

Kirkwood’s Indy 500 finishes with Andretti Global are 28th, seventh, 32nd and 16th, respectively. He also pointed to short ovals as areas where he can find additional performance.

“Maybe cleaning up some of the short oval stuff,” Kirkwood said. “Maybe even some of the road-course stuff we can get better at.”

Kirkwood (photo, above) made significant progress in 2026. He recorded 15 top-10 finishes in 18 starts in the No. 27 Sam’s Club Honda. He had 10 top-10s in 17 starts in 2025 and 13 in 17 starts in 2024.

The biggest difference came in the quality of those finishes. Kirkwood recorded 10 top-fives this season after posting five in each of the previous two years. His six podium finishes also matched his combined total from his first 68 INDYCAR SERIES starts.

The consistency helped make 2026 Kirkwood’s strongest season, even though he won fewer races than he did in 2025.

Kirkwood won three times last season but finished outside the top five in 12 of his 17 starts. This year, he turned more of his opportunities into strong finishes, winning twice, and avoided the mistakes that can derail a championship run.

“I think things are just starting to click,” Kirkwood said.

Andretti Global also showed more strength as an organization during the second half of the season. Will Power and Marcus Ericsson produced consistent results alongside Kirkwood, giving the team multiple cars near the front of the field.

“You shine when you have all three cars up there,” Kirkwood said. “Our performance was starting to show as the second part of the season came around.”

Andretti Global has not won an NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship since Ryan Hunter-Reay in 2012. Kirkwood’s runner-up finish puts the organization closer to that goal, but the next step requires more performance at the tracks where Palou has been strongest.

Kirkwood knows where to look.

“Yeah, across the board we’re solid,” he said. “Getting better every season. It’s just little things now that will make the difference in the championship. We have a lot of momentum going into the offseason. We have a direction.”

title: Inside Line: How Will 2026 Season Be Most Remembered?
excerpt:
Featured

SEP 16, 2026

Today’s question: For what will the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season be most remembered?

Curt Cavin: This was a memorable year on many levels, and I’m sure the fellas participating in this roundtable will highlight some of them. But the last lap of a spectacular Indianapolis 500 (photo, top) likely will stand as an all-time Indy moment, and it should. Felix Rosenqvist took the green flag in third place behind Marcus Armstrong and David Malukas, then spent nearly a full lap dangerously side by side with Armstrong, his teammate at Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian. The more I watch Rosenqvist’s in-car camera, the more breathtaking the action becomes. Rosenqvist cleared Armstrong in Turn 4 and set his sights on Malukas, drawing closer in the draft before sweeping to the outside for the pass to register the closest finish in event history (.0233 of a second). Rosenqvist called the lap “gnarly,” and he described his driving as an out-of-body experience. I believe it. It was incredible action, and you’ll see the replays long after those of other big moments from the 2026 season.

Eric Smith: My moment was Scott Dixon leaving Chip Ganassi Racing after 25 years. He earned 58 of his 59 victories and all six of his championships with the team, so seeing Dixon (photo, above) announced in early July as leaving CGR was a huge moment with seismic implications. A week later, he was announced as joining Arrow McLaren. That announcement also included reigning Indianapolis 500 winner Felix Rosenqvist joining Dixon at Arrow McLaren. Rosenqvist had a highlight-reel season and really found his footing with Meyer Shank Racing, only to announce less than two months later that he was leaving and returning to McLaren. That move left Christian Lundgaard, a top-three driver throughout the season who won twice, without a seat. Silly Season was very silly this year, with marquee names moving all over the grid.

Arni Sribhen: I agree with Curt. The 2026 Indianapolis 500 will be the thing that the 2026 season will be best remembered for, but I’ll also remember it for the three new events that hit the calendar this season. Arlington set the standard for what an INDYCAR street race should be. It was a return to a big market, and it delivered a Texas-sized event. Markham showed potential to be a solid replacement for downtown Toronto’s Exhibition Place, and the Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, D.C. (photo, above), was an event that few who attended will ever forget. Year two for Arlington and Markham should be even better. Hopefully, the schedule will allow for a return to D.C., as well.

Paul Kelly: Curt, Eric and Arni all made strong points for indelible moments this season. But I’ll remember 2026 as the year Alex Palou moved into the foothills of the Mount Rushmore of the sport with his fourth consecutive series championship and fifth in six years. He already is the youngest five-time champion in the century-plus history of INDYCAR SERIES racing. It’s no longer a question whether Palou (photo, above) is a legend of the sport. The question now is when he will enter the GOAT (Greatest of All Time) discussion if he continues to win races and titles at this pace. And don’t count on anyone topping Palou before the new IR-28 car is introduced for the 2028 season, either. His No. 10 Chip Ganassi Racing team has figured out the technical and strategic puzzle of the current equipment package better than any other, and that, combined with Palou’s sublime driving skill, will deliver a record-setting fifth straight title and sixth overall in 2027.

title: Dennis Hauger Joins AJ Foyt Racing for 2027
excerpt:
AJ Foyt Racing has signed 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year Dennis Hauger to a multiyear agreement beginning with the 2027 season.

Hauger, 23, joins AJ Foyt Racing after completing his first NTT INDYCAR SERIES season with Dale Coyne Racing. He will drive the No. 14 Homes For Our Troops Chevrolet.

The Norwegian came to the United States for the 2025 INDY NXT by Firestone season and made an immediate impact, winning six races and the championship with Andretti Global.

Before coming to America, Hauger progressed through the European open-wheel ranks. He won the 2019 Italian Formula 4 championship and the 2021 FIA Formula 3 title before moving to Formula 2, where he won five races. He also was a longtime member of the Red Bull Junior Team.

AJ Foyt Racing Team President Larry Foyt said Hauger’s experience and ability to adapt quickly made him an important addition as the team prepares for 2027 and beyond.

“Dennis has accomplished a lot for someone who is only 23,” Foyt said. “Every time he’s moved into something new, he’s adapted quickly and he’s won. Coming over here and winning in INDY NXT as a rookie certainly got everyone’s attention, and then we watched how he progressed through his rookie season in INDYCAR.”

Hauger said he is looking forward to joining AJ Foyt Racing and continuing his development in the No. 14 Chevrolet.

“I’m really excited about it,” Hauger said. “Larry and I have had some very good conversations about the team and where they want to go. I’ve learned a lot in my first two years racing in America, but I still feel like there is a lot more for me to learn and accomplish in INDYCAR.

“This team has so much history in this sport, but what intrigues me even more was hearing about the future and what they’re building now. I want to work hard with everyone there and see how far we can take it.”

Hauger’s signing is part of AJ Foyt Racing’s plan to build on the foundation established by team founder A.J. Foyt.

“We’ve spent a lot of time talking about where we want this team to go,” Foyt said. “We’re investing in our people, our technical side and our commercial program because we want to continue moving forward. Dennis is a big part of that plan.

“We’re fortunate to have partners like Hendricks Holding Company and Homes For Our Troops who believe in what we’re doing with the No. 14 program. They’ve given us the opportunity to keep building, and now it’s our job to make the most of it.”

Hauger will make his first public appearance with AJ Foyt Racing on Oct. 2 at the GM Defense Valor & Velocity Gala at the GM Design Dome in Warren, Michigan. The Homes For Our Troops car will be on display at the event, which supports the Medal of Honor Foundation and will bring together senior GM leadership, military leaders and members of the U.S. defense community.

Diane Hendricks and her daughter, Konya Hendricks Schuh, of Hendricks Holding Company Inc., also will attend, along with Gen. (USA, Ret.) Richard A. Cody, chairman of the board of Homes For Our Troops, and Brig. Gen. (USA, Ret.) Tom Landwermeyer, president and CEO of Homes For Our Troops.

Homes For Our Troops builds and donates specially adapted custom homes for severely injured post-9/11 veterans. The organization has been represented throughout the 2026 season on Foyt’s No. 14 Chevrolet.

“I’ve been learning more about Homes For Our Troops and what the No. 14 HFOT.org car represents,” Hauger said. “It’s obviously much bigger than racing, and I’m looking forward to meeting General Cody, Diane and Konya and learning more about it. To have my first event with the team connected to Homes For Our Troops and supporting the Medal of Honor Foundation makes it a pretty special way to get started.”

The Oct. 2 gala will give Hauger an opportunity to meet many of the people behind the No. 14 program before AJ Foyt Racing turns its attention to preparing for the 2027 season.

Hauger’s signing is the first of additional announcements expected from AJ Foyt Racing regarding its 2027 driver lineup in the coming weeks.

“Dennis wants to win, and we want to win,” Foyt said. “That’s where everything starts.”

title: IR-28 Remains On Target in Development After IMS Oval Test
excerpt:
Mission accomplished. The two Dallara IR-28 validation tests at Indianapolis Motor Speedway delivered what INDYCAR needed most: data.

Alexander Rossi and Alex Palou drove the NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ next-generation car on the 2.439-mile, 14-turn IMS road course across three days in early August. Last week, they returned to the 2.5-mile oval for two days of testing in superspeedway configuration.

Rossi represented Chevrolet and ECR during both tests, Palou, a five-time series champion, represented Honda and Chip Ganassi Racing. Rossi won the 2016 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. Palou won the “500” in 2025.

The tests focused on validation rather than speed. The IR-28 (photo, above) doesn’t debut until the 2028 season, giving INDYCAR and Dallara time to understand how the car responds to different configurations, conditions and setup changes. The road-course test established the baseline. The oval test introduced a different set of demands.

The road-course configuration generates the grip needed for heavy braking and cornering. The superspeedway configuration reduces drag so the car can move efficiently through the air and remain stable at high speeds.

“The biggest things that are different (between the two configurations) really are the front and rear wings,” said Mike O’Gara, INDYCAR’s vice president of competition and race engineering.

The road-course car uses larger front and rear wings to generate downforce. The superspeedway car uses smaller wings to reduce drag.

INDYCAR and Dallara also spent much of the superspeedway test studying aerodynamic sensitivity and ride height.

“You can take a turn of front wing out or a turn of rear wing and how that affects the aerodynamic balance,” O’Gara said. “We also worked a lot with ride heights of the car to see where its sweet spot is.”

Ride height measures the distance between the car and the track surface. INDYCAR SERIES machinery runs extremely close to the ground because the space beneath the car plays an important role in generating aerodynamic performance.

The oval places greater demands on that aerodynamic platform. The car runs at high speed for much of the lap, and small changes in its attitude can affect the balance between the front and rear of the car.

“One of the design goals with this car was to make it a lot less sensitive on ride height, which means it should race better,” O’Gara said. “It should be less susceptible to elements, air temperature and track temp.”

Conditions Sept. 9 at IMS put that objective to the test. Temperatures climbed into the low 90s, with high humidity, as Rossi completed the first day of superspeedway testing. INDYCAR and Dallara used the conditions to make significant setup changes and measure the car’s response.

“We made some big swings,” O’Gara said. “With the current car, you change the front and rear ride height by a millimeter or two. We were making 5- and 6-millimeter swings just to make big changes to see how it affects the car.”

Rossi (photo, above) felt the changes in the car and provided feedback that matched the data.

“I couldn’t ask for much more right now,” O’Gara said.

Palou tested the following day in conditions roughly 10 degrees cooler, with less humidity. The weather more closely resembled the conditions teams typically encounter during the Month of May, giving INDYCAR another set of data. O’Gara compared the two-day test to compressing an entire Month of May practice program into a much shorter window.

“When teams unload here during that month, they start conservative, and each day they get a little more aggressive,” he said. “We’re doing the same thing. We’re just trying to make sure the deltas are correct. When we do make a downforce change, the number makes sense, and we get the balance back to where it needs to be.”

Dallara and INDYCAR also used the test to compare track data with its wind tunnel predictions.

“That’s what this test was, a whole list of Dallara parts on and off the car and seeing if those numbers match their wind tunnel data,” O’Gara said. “Everything went as planned. Didn’t miss a beat.”

The new car also avoided the types of issues that can emerge during an initial track test. O’Gara (photo, above, right) said the IR-28 experienced no unexpected interference between components.

“We got good data and just put in laps and learning as we go,” he said.

The data revealed another important characteristic of the IR-28: speed. Indianapolis is synonymous with speed. While not chasing it, everyone wondered.

The new car will use a 2.4-liter twin-turbocharged V6 internal combustion engine capable of producing up to 760 horsepower. The engine formula will increase torque and power compared to the current NTT INDYCAR SERIES engines.

An evolved low-voltage hybrid system will accompany the new engine. It will provide greater energy storage and expanded deployment options while reducing the power unit’s weight by approximately 20 pounds compared to the current generation. Chevrolet and Honda have committed to the new engine formula.

The additional power, combined with the lighter and more efficient IR-28 package, could bring one of the most recognizable records in INDYCAR SERIES history into range. Arie Luyendyk set the four-lap qualifying record at IMS on May 12, 1996, with an average speed of 236.986 mph. He also established the single-lap record that day at 237.498 mph.

The IR-28 was not chasing those records last week at IMS. INDYCAR was using the test to establish performance targets and validate the car’s design. But the early data provided encouragement.

“Basically, we went a certain speed during this test with how much power we’re going to need with this configuration,” O’Gara said. “We’re to a point where we can go back to the OEMs (Honda and Chevrolet) and say, ‘Here’s your horsepower targets to hit,’ and they’ll go away and do their science and engineering stuff and come back and tell us whether that’s achievable or not.

“But we think with the 2.4-liter that they will be bringing, I think those targets are achievable. Numbers are correlating with the wind tunnel and with all their other design parameters. So far, so good.”

title: Swedish Hometown To Honor Rosenqvist With Public Celebration
excerpt:
Track News

SEP 15, 2026

2026 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Felix Rosenqvist will be honored Saturday, Dec. 5 by his hometown, Värnamo, during a public celebration in the Swedish city.

Local residents, motorsports fans and visitors from near and far are invited to join the city in celebrating his historic victory May 24 in the Indianapolis 500. The free, family-friendly event will take place in central Värnamo with Rosenqvist as the guest of honor.

“Celebrating an Indy 500 victory in my hometown will be an unforgettable way to conclude the best year of my life,” Rosenqvist said. “Sharing an occasion like this with everyone in Värnamo, where the dream began, will feel completely surreal. It will truly be one of those pinch-me moments.

“It is truly amazing to think that we will all be able to experience and share this together. I am really looking forward to seeing friends, family and everyone else in Värnamo in December.”

The program will include tributes from the stage, interviews, live music and motorsports-themed activities. Representatives from INDYCAR will take part in the celebration. Additional news and highlights will be announced closer to the event.

Rosenqvist earned his first victory in ”The Greatest Spectacle in Racing” in the No. 60 Honda for Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian. He beat David Malukas of Team Penske by .0233 of a second in the closest finish in the century-plus history of the race.

“Felix Rosenqvist’s success is an outstanding achievement that has inspired tremendous pride and joy throughout Värnamo,” said Staffan Svensson, project manager and destination development officer at Värnamo Municipality. ”We want to give the people of Värnamo and the motorsports community an opportunity to celebrate him together, while also showcasing the strong sense of community and local pride that exists here.”

The event is being jointly organized by Värnamo Näringsliv, Värnamo City and Värnamo Municipality.

“This partnership reflects the strong sense of community that makes Värnamo what it is,” said Anki Hansson of Värnamo Näringsliv. ”Together, we want to create a public celebration that honors Felix while also welcoming visitors to Värnamo.”

title: Barry Wanser Weaves Even More Magic With Tight-Knit Palou Team
excerpt:
A group of brothers is how Barry Wanser, strategist for Alex Palou, describes the No. 10 DHL Chip Ganassi Racing team. It’s a group that guided Palou to his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship and fourth consecutive title this season.

Wanser believes its success goes beyond the numbers. The team has spent the past several seasons learning what makes Palou tick and, more importantly, what he needs to perform at his best.

It’s a recipe everyone tries to replicate but can’t. So, how does this team continue this dominance?

Wanser (photo, top, with Palou) has worked with the No. 10 car since 2004 and has led its race weekend strategy since team owner Chip Ganassi moved to Scott Dixon’s timing stand in 2018. He helped Dan Wheldon win six races and Dario Franchitti win 13 races and three consecutive championships.

Wanser (photo, above) sees something different in Palou that makes him stand out. He sees a driver who understands what he needs from a race car, communicates that to his engineers and adapts when circumstances change.

“It’s the relationship he’s been able to form with the team,” Wanser said. “Specifically with his race engineer, Julian Robertson. That ability that they have to extract and make changes to really get the extra performance out of the car that Alex needs to get the fuel mileage with a lap time to take care of the tires to then go perform at the highest level. Everyone says we’ve made it look easy and stuff. It’s by far not easy.”

Wanser admits Palou’s understanding of the car is just as important. On road and street courses, he knows what the car needs to perform on both the primary and alternate Firestone Firehawk tires. On ovals, he understands the differences between a car built for qualifying and one built for racing.

“Trying to get those done and understand that with the very short amount of practice that we actually get is a challenge,” Wanser said. “That’s something that he’s been able to adapt to in the last few years, especially the oval performance and what it takes.”

A team can give a driver a great car. Engineers can provide the tools, and strategists can make the calls. The driver still must put everything together, and Palou has consistently done that while developing a relationship with the people around him that allows the entire group to function at its highest level.

That was particularly important during the 2026 season. The No. 10 team dealt with strategy missteps, pit-lane speeding, contact with other teams’ equipment and bad pit stops. Each created an opportunity for the championship to slip away.

The team kept recovering.

“It’s really easy to get it wrong, so it’s very hard what we do,” Wanser said. “But for all of Chip Ganassi Racing, the engineers have just really done an incredible job. Everywhere we go, the cars have unloaded very strong, and then it’s up to the individual race engineers with their drivers to extract that extra performance out of the cars, make those changes.”

Palou has 25 career victories, including six in the 2026 season. Wanser believes Palou’s ability to take information, process it and turn it into performance is a major part of that success. Another part is harder to quantify.

Trust.

Palou, Robertson, Wanser and the rest of the No. 10 crew have developed an understanding since Palou joined Chip Ganassi Racing in 2021. They communicate quickly and honestly, which matters in a series where there is little room for error.

Wanser understands that dynamic better than most. He retired from his full-time role as senior manager of racing operations at Chip Ganassi Racing after last season but remained Palou’s strategist. The decision was part of a four- or five-year plan he developed with Ganassi and managing director Mike Hull to mentor Blair Julian and Mike LeGallic and prepare them for greater responsibilities at the Indianapolis shop and at the track.

Wanser (photo, above, white shirt) and his wife, Laurie, moved from Indiana to Florida during last year’s offseason. He and Palou began the 2026 season in Wanser’s new home state on the streets of St. Petersburg, where they won the season opener.

“I take a lot of pride knowing that my family’s plan to move to Florida last year was set in motion four years prior,” Wanser said. “The last time to mentor people, get other people in place, and that’s what you want rather than just say, ‘Hey, the end of this year, I’m going to be moving.’

“So, obviously with what I do on race day, it’s a big part of still the performance of the team. To be able to still be able to do that is an amazing situation for me.

“I’ve been here 29 years, and I’ve been on the 10-car pit stand since 2004. It would be a lot of experience that would just walk away, and I don’t want that.”

Those 29 years have taught Wanser that success is never one person.

Wanser is quick to point out that Ganassi and Palou deserve a higher level of credit, but everyone on the team has a role in allowing the driver to perform at his best. The strategist is simply the person responsible for making the final call.

“For us on the stand, it’s easy,” Wanser said. “I get too much credit as a strategist because it’s not just me. I manage the process. I learned that from Chip many years ago. Yes, ultimately you make the final decision. But generally, we’re constantly talking about strategy, and nine times out of 10, we’re all in agreement what we’re going to do. But sometimes we’re not, and I have to decide.”

That dynamic may be the best explanation for Palou’s remarkable run. His talent is undeniable, but he is surrounded by people he trusts. He listens, communicates and understands what the car needs. Then he goes out and executes at a level that can make one of the most difficult jobs in motorsports look easy.

“We’re a group of brothers,” Wanser said. “We’re having fun. If you say something dumb, you’re going to be made fun of. No one’s off-limits, like myself included. We just have fun.

“If things aren’t going right, we blame each other, kind of thing. But in a fun way, not in an accusing way. Literally, we just roll with it. Everyone knows they’re trying to do the best they can, and we’re having a lot of fun.

“We have no idea how long this amazing amount of success will continue, but we’re just enjoying every bit of it and having fun along the way here.”

title: FOX INDYCAR Coverage Scores Second Straight Year of Big Growth
excerpt:
Broadcasts Attract 23% Gain Over 2025, 57% Hike Over 2024

FOX Sports announced Sept. 11 its blistering momentum with the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, averaging 1,681,000 viewers per race, an increase of 23 percent over last year’s full-season average (1,362,000 for 17 races), according to Nielsen Media Research.

The ratings also increased by 57% vs. 2024’s full-season average on NBC (1,073,000 for 16 races), good for the best viewership since 2008. Additionally, FOX INDYCAR scored nine races with at least 1 million viewers, the most since 2008 (10).

Highlights among the events broadcast by FOX were the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 (6,635,000 viewers), the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. (3,282,000), and the XPEL Grand Prix of Road America (1,803,000).

Fast Start, New Events Highlight 2026 Coverage

The FOX INDYCAR season got off the starting line with a stronger schedule than in 2025, slotting in three consecutive races -- and four total – in March, including a doubleheader with NASCAR in Phoenix with the Good Ranchers 250 (1,247,000 viewers) and the debut of the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (1,336,000 viewers), teaming with the Dallas Cowboys and Texas Rangers on the world-class, Texas-sized event.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. added a tentpole event of epic proportion in August, with the FOX audience peaking at nearly 3.5 million viewers and delivering media coverage from around the world. The race was the most-watched non-Indianapolis 500 INDYCAR SERIES event since 1995.

Key Demos Continue To Grow

FOX INDYCAR coverage saw a second consecutive year of growth in the coveted P18-49 audience demographic, according to Nielsen Media Research.

The 2026 season finished up 10% vs. 2025 (341,000 vs. 310,000) and up 66% vs. 2024 (205,000). Also in 2026, P25-54 was up 15% vs. last year (412,000 vs. 358,000) and up 63% vs. 2024 (253,000).

Digital Coverage Also Popular

“ALL IN: INDYCAR,” the real-time, season-long documentary series produced by FOX Sports, INDYCAR and Shadow Lion, the critically acclaimed creative studio co-founded by Tom Brady, scored more than 6 million views on YouTube in its first season, averaging nearly 500,000 viewers an episode. The series has been confirmed for a second season in 2027.

Also in 2026, the debut season of “SPEED WITH HARVICK AND BUXTON FUELED BY POET” amassed more than 100 million views on FOX Sports social and digital platforms, making it the fastest ever to hit that mark on FOX Sports platforms. The original digital program also eclipsed 200,000 followers across FOX Sports social and digital platforms.

In August, FOX Sports Digital delivered full coverage of the Freedom 250 across social and editorial, which ranked as the most-viewed non-Indianapolis 500 race week of the INDYCAR SERIES season on social (21 million views) and the highest time spent reading on editorial (5:31).

INDY NXT by Firestone Also Grows Double Digits

The INDY NXT by Firestone season averaged 127,000 viewers (17 races on FS1/FS2), up 14% vs. last year's full-season average (111,000 viewers for 14 races), according to Nielsen Media Research.

The top-three highest-viewership races were Mid-Ohio 1 with 250,000 viewers (July 4), Barber 1 with 191,000 (March 28) and Arlington with 176,000 (March 15).
